reason: In the supplied assembly, each K step has separate A and B pointer increments, then four FMOPA operations and loop control. That is a concrete address-generation and control cost to investigate; it does not establish a performance bottleneck or predict a speedup. I rank narrow changes to the inner loop first. Prior preload, pointer-end, and two-step-unroll trials did not qualify for promotion, so related scheduling proposals rank lower. Packing and traversal changes add more correctness risk and timed work. Register reuse ranks last because the current loop already loads each operand pair once and reuses it across four FMOPA operations, so the proposal does not describe a distinct change.
